correspondence.finding: The northeastern opening follows an eastern feeder into the Captain Grant Creek-side corridor, around its northward elbow into the Skaist River drainage. The Skaist corridor continues southwest to Highway 3 and joins the Skagit. The selected route then turns south through the upper Skagit valley into Ross Lake across the international border, continues through Ross, Diablo and Gorge lake settings, and follows the Skagit downstream toward Newhalem. The Canadian original resolves the headward junction sequence rather than relying on a nearby basin label.
correspondence.limits: Initial small feeder and exact Captain Grant/Skaist/Skagit naming transitions are not assigned vertex boundaries. Reservoir centerlines are component context, not proof that a river name is a scalar label for the impoundments. Ordinary generalized river/lake rendering does not prevent component correspondence.

correspondence.finding: The southwestward Skagit valley from the Newhalem surroundings through the Marblemount/Cascade River joining setting to the Rockport/Sauk joining setting is continuously visible in the original cartography and corresponds to this complete middle feature.
correspondence.limits: Cascade River is adjoining context, not an additional selected branch or alias. Feature-break locations do not adjudicate name changes.

correspondence.finding: From the Sauk junction the selection follows the Skagit west through the Concrete and lower-valley settings, past Sedro-Woolley/Burlington and Mount Vernon, then turns onto the mapped North Fork Skagit River branch to its Skagit Bay outlet. The chosen western delta outlet is distinguished from the more southerly South Fork Skagit branch.
correspondence.limits: The selected terminal supports a coastal North Fork Skagit outlet context. No contemporary shoreline intersection, surveyed mouth vertex, tidal condition or exhaustive distributary inventory is assigned.

correspondence.finding: The southeastern headward approach follows the Sloan Creek-side corridor north and northwest into North Fork Sauk River, then the Sauk past its South Fork and White Chuck joining settings and toward the Darrington/lower Sauk corridor. All of the selected upper tributary feature is covered by the full-area and focused original views.
correspondence.limits: The initial small feeder, exact Sloan Creek/North Fork Sauk/Sauk name-change vertices and natural source are not individually adjudicated. North Fork Skykomish and other adjacent drainages are not substituted for the connected selected branch.

correspondence.finding: This is the northward lower Sauk continuation of fid 9417, through the Suiattle joining setting to the Sauk–Skagit junction near Rockport. The map shows the trunk and joining context continuously.
correspondence.limits: The two tributary feature IDs are successive modeled pieces of one Sauk-side branch, not evidence of two independent natural tributaries. Suiattle is a separate adjoining tributary and is not itself selected in full.

correspondence.component_scope: South Fork opening and inland wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected headward route is South Fork Edisto southeast of Johnston, through the Aiken–Denmark–Bamberg swamp corridor. McTier and Shaw creeks are adjoining tributaries rather than the selected main headward route.
The selected South Fork meets North Fork near Branchville and continues as Edisto. Four Hole Swamp joins farther downstream above the Givhans southward bend.

correspondence.component_scope: Tidal South Edisto and neighboring coastal arms
correspondence.finding: The selected lower setting lies on the South Edisto side west of Edisto Island, toward St. Helena Sound. North Edisto and Dawho form a distinct connected eastern coastal arm and are not substituted for the selected southward continuation.
All of the generalized corridor is covered with no material connector remaining. The strongly generalized displayed seaward extension is not an exact channel trace or surveyed natural river mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Andean headward path into the northeastern Babahoyo drainage
correspondence.finding: The regional map places the path in the east-west headwater network above Moraspungo/Quinsaloma and the Zapotal approach. Several nearby tributaries cannot be separated continuously at the acquired map resolution.
correspondence.material_gap: The initial eastern feeder and its connection into the downstream selected trunk are not continuously established; this is not just uncertainty about an exact name boundary.

correspondence.finding: The selected long southward course corresponds regionally to the mapped corridor from the Ventanas area through the Catarama/Caracol reach toward Babahoyo.
correspondence.correspondence: supported generalized corridor; no legal name-boundary assignment

correspondence.finding: The southwestward continuation below Babahoyo is represented on the regional drainage map and belongs to the Babahoyo receiving branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Babahoyo, Guayaquil junction and Guayas terminal reach
correspondence.finding: CELEC cartography resolves the broad lower Babahoyo/Daule/Guayas setting. The regional map continues the Guayas channel southward past Guayaquil and Santay toward the selected lower-estuarine ending.
correspondence.correspondence: supported receiving corridor and broad terminal setting
correspondence.limits: The selected ending is an internal model terminal in the broad Guayas estuarine channel; it is not established as the actual ocean mouth. Exact channel edges and tidal limits are outside this finding.

correspondence.finding: The two adjacent CELEC sheets show the eastern Chimbo course passing south of Milagro and turning northwest through Yaguachi toward the Babahoyo junction, matching the selected generalized feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Short eastern feeder immediately north of Quevedo
correspondence.finding: The regional map shows eastern drainage reaching the Quevedo corridor around the Valencia/La Esperanza area, but the short selected feeder cannot be securely distinguished from adjoining branches.
correspondence.material_gap: Independent legible branch-specific coverage is needed for the whole small feeder and junction. No Toachi or San Pablo name is assigned from proximity.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern eastward headwater and return bend
correspondence.finding: The regional map shows several eastern-draining coastal-hill tributaries above the Daule reservoir, including the Río de Oro vicinity. Its acquired pixels do not securely establish the selected whole eastward path and subsequent northward return connection.
correspondence.material_gap: Actual selected headward branch and its joining course remain unestablished; Río de Oro is only a geographically plausible lead, not an accepted component attribution.

correspondence.component_scope: Western impoundment passage and downstream Daule approach
correspondence.finding: HGG01 shows the large western impoundment landscape; the operator report establishes Daule-Peripa and downstream Daule continuity. The selected whole through-reservoir route was not independently resolved.
correspondence.correspondence: reservoir setting supported; connector material pending
correspondence.material_gap: Needs legible independent coverage connecting the selected upper arm through the reservoir to the downstream Daule course, without assuming the modeled line proves flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and lower Daule to Guayaquil
correspondence.finding: Regional cartography and operator prose support the Daule corridor through the Balzar/Santa Lucía/Daule valley. CELEC maps resolve its lower approach and junction in the Guayaquil setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern headward bend and Baba-side chain
correspondence.finding: The northern regional map contains a dense feeder network south of Santo Domingo. The operator notice establishes a Baba/Toachi reservoir-to-Quevedo relationship, but does not select this particular upper bend or every connector.
correspondence.material_gap: The eastern headward feeder, northwest turn and onward connection through the Baba-side system need continuous source correspondence. No claim that the entire feature is Baba is made.

correspondence.finding: The regional map supports the north-south receiving corridor toward Quevedo, while operator prose independently links Baba outflow with Quevedo. This does not establish every upstream feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Quevedo–Vinces chain and selected lower eastern turn
correspondence.finding: The regional map supports Quevedo, Mocache and Vinces along the central chain. The selected lower continuation and eastward connection within the divided lowland drainage are not continuously distinguishable on the acquired map.
correspondence.correspondence: upper/middle corridor supported; lower branch material pending
correspondence.material_gap: Needs branch-specific correspondence below Vinces through the selected return toward Babahoyo; basin membership alone does not establish that connector.

correspondence.finding: The independent raster shows a terrain of narrow stream valleys and small lakes. The selected generalized path can be followed through the same valley/channel network around the inland uplands, including the broad westward turn and subsequent northward passage. Local simplified vertices and stream-bank positions differ, but no genuinely missing corridor connector was found.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale
correspondence.name_limit: No readable hydronym establishes a name for this upstream feeder or whole loop.

correspondence.component_scope: northward lake-linked reach and northeast middle corridor
correspondence.finding: Overlapping source views show the elongated northward water corridor, the connecting small-lake/channel landscape around the eastward bend, and the larger northeast valley continuing downstream. The middle turn is represented by mapped connected waterways, not merely by the proximity of a regional name label. No uncovered connector remains between the overlapping views.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The selected lower corridor corresponds to the mapped river entering a broad braided, marshy inlet-head tract and continuing along its northwestern side toward open water. Source cartography displays several terminal channels. The generalized endpoint belongs to this coastal setting; no exact branch, bank, surveyed mouth point, tidal limit or current flow state is claimed. ARC 403 chapter 10, printed page 10-4, paragraph 53 independently describes a broad braided stream entering the swampy head of Richard Collinson Inlet.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale
